title: Proof on Broadway starring Ayo Edebiri and Don Cheadle #proofbroadway...
transcript: In a stunning Broadway debut, Ayo Edebiri leads a simple but quality revival of Proof by David Auburn. She plays Catherine, the 25-year-old daughter of a brilliant and mentally ill mathematician, here played by Don Cheadle. In the aftermath of her father's death, Catherine grapples with what she has potentially inherited from him — elements of his genius and his instability. I thought this was a really great production and found it in remarkable shape for a third preview. Ayo Edebiri's performance is funny and layered as she physicalizes Catherine differently depending on the context of a given scene. She's also very expressive with her eyes, capturing internal realizations and pointed reactions with a distinct but not exaggerated clarity. She effortlessly transitions between the humorous and more emotional moments, and has solid chemistry with everyone in the cast, especially the always-transcendent Kara Young, who plays her sister. Producing this play with a primarily Black cast opens up some really interesting dimensions to the story and its themes as it relates to the way the characters address mental illness or how they conceptualize what genius is, for example. Proof is kind of a deceptively simple piece, requiring nuance and balance to make it shine. Everyone here delivers and in the charmingly intimate Booth Theatre, every seat affords you the opportunity to appreciate the details. I was sitting partial view on a $49 lottery seat and it was honestly great — a steal, actually. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
